🧪 Effects 🧪

Author: iDexy
Translator: Zivkovic
Writer: iDexy

In this channel all effects of the game are listed and explained how they influence the player

Category 1: 📖 Basic Things 📖

- An effect is a helpful or harmful condition that affects an entity. Effects can be inflicted in various ways throughout the game, including consuming potions and some food items, being in the range of beacons and conduits, and being attacked by or close to certain mobs

- The /effect command allows players to inflict effects upon themselves and other entities

- You can get them with Normal potions, splash potions lingering potions and tipped arrows

- To use normal potions, you just drink the potion. To use splash potions, throw the potion to the ground to get the effect of the potion. To use lingering potions, throw the potion to the ground or a block to create an effect cloud with the effect of that potion

❗ IMPORTANT ❗

- If you have splash potions, throw the potion up in the air to get the maximum power of the potion (the effect will last longer)

- When a creeper has an effect and explodes, it leaves an area effect cloud for each effect that it had before it died

- Players can open their inventory to see any current effects afflicted upon them, as well as its level and duration

- However, it is not possible to apply the same effect multiple times, even if they are of different levels (e.g. Strength and Strength 2)

- Positive effects have blue text in potion information, and in are displayed on the upper row of effects in the heads up display, while negative effects have red potion text and are displayed in the bottom row. Neutral effects have the blue potion text and are listed with the negative effects in the bottom row in the heads up display
.

Category 2: 🩺 Behaviour 🩺

Basic Things:

- Any entities inflicted by an effect are affected in various ways for an amount of time

- During the effect, spiral-shaped particles emanate from the position of the inflicted entity

- For most effects, higher levels increase the strength of the effect

❗ IMPORTANT ❗

- Note that even with commands, effects cannot be made to last forever. If an effect is set to last a time greater than 32766 (215−2) ticks, 27 minutes and 18 seconds, or 1638 seconds, it displays as ^^.^^, but still continues ticking down and eventually expires
.

- Any number of different effects, including opposing effects such as Strength and Weakness, can be simultaneously active on a player

- When the stronger effect then overrides the weaker effect, the weaker effect remains, but is hidden. It returns after the stronger effect expires, if the weaker effect has a higher duration than the stronger effect. This change makes it impossible to create custom potion antidotes by applying an amplified effect with a one tick duration

- All effects can be removed by drinking milk, dying, being saved from death by a totem of undying, or traveling through the return portal in the End
.

Category 4: 📖 🧪 Explanation Of Effects 🧪 📖

In this category we will explain the effects in more detail by following the following points:

1. Description

2. Causes

Let's follow the order of the summary effects:

🥾 Speed 🥾

1. Description - Speed is a status effect that increases an entity's walking speed by +20% multiplied by the effect level. It expands a player's field of view (FOV) accordingly. You can find 2 levels:

Level 1-> +20% Speed
Level 2-> +40% Speed

❗ IMPORTANT ❗

- Moving with speed 2 takes less exhaustion on the same distance because you don't need to jump
- Your FOV increases when you have speed effect but you can disable in the accessibility settings

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Speed Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- With speed 1 your faster while jumping and with speed 2 your faster without jumps

- Witches drink the Potion of Swiftness if their target is over 11 blocks away

- The cause of ¨Spawning within the world¨ lasts for 3 years, 4 months, 25 days, 6 hours, 45 minutes, and 42.4 seconds, or (2^31)-1 ticks. Only spiders can have this

- With a beacon set to Speed, your speed effect replenishes when in range. Getting 2 effects at once requires beacon pyramid level 4

🐢 Slowness 🐢

1. Description - Slowness decreases walking speed by -15% × level and contracts the player's field of view accordingly. Negative levels of Slowness increase walking speed. However, sprinting and jumping is barely affected. You can find 6 levels:

Level 1-> -15% Walking Speed
Level 2-> -30% Walking Speed
Level 3-> -45% Walking Speed
Level 4-> -60% Walking Speed
Level 5-> -75% Walking Speed
Level 6-> -90% Walking Speed

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Slowness Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- Witches may throw Splash Potion of Slowness if their target is at least 8 blocks away

- The Arrows of Slowness have 50% chance of being dropped by Strays

- The Arrows of Slowness (extended) are fired by Strays

⛏️ Haste ⛏️

1. Description - Haste is a status effect that increases attack speed by +10% x level and increases mining speed by +20% x level. Negative levels decrease mining and attack speed, similar to Mining Fatigue. However, the attack speed increases are purely visual. You can find 2 levels:

Level 1-> +10% Attack Speed. +20% Mining Speed
Level 2-> +20% Attack Speed. +40% Mining Speed

❗ IMPORTANT ❗

- Keep in mind that Mining Fatigue 3 inflicted by elder guardians prevents the player from instant mining most blocks regardless of the Haste effect, along with a huge decrease of mining speed. However, lower levels of Mining Fatigue can be overcome by Haste of level III or greater, with a resultant reduced Haste effect

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Haste Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- With a beacon set to Haste, your haste effect replenishes when in range. Getting 2 effects at once requires beacon pyramid level 4

🥄 Mining Fatigue 🥄

1. Description - The effect decreases attack speed by -10% × level, equivalent to the attack speed cooldown attribute decreasing by -0.2 × level. For the in-game default level 3, attack speed decreases by -30% (attack speed cooldown attribute decreases by -0.6), and it takes ~370 times longer than usual to break a block with the proper tool for that block. It decreases also the mining speed. You can find 4 levels:

Level 1-> -10% Attack Speed. -70% Mining Speed
Level 2-> -20% Attack Speed. -91% Mining Speed
Level 3-> -30% Attack Speed. -99.73% Mining Speed
Level 4-> -40% Attack Speed. -99.919% Mining Speed

While afflicted, a player can still craft and ride entities as usual, but cannot remove most vehicles due to how slowly the vehicle can be broken

The affliction is cured by drinking milk, although milk does not prevent a subsequent affliction by an elder guardian, which can happen within a few seconds. Axolotls can also remove this effect

2. Causes - The only natural cause of Mining Fatigue is from affliction by an elder guardian, and the only natural effect level is 3. Other levels can be achieved via commands

Once per minute, elder guardians in the vicinity search for any player within 50 blocks to afflict with Mining Fatigue 3. A player cannot defend from this attack. Concealment behind blocks, underground, or by a potion of Invisibility offers no defense. The length of this effect is 5:00 minutes
.

🩸 Strength 🩸

1. Description - Increases melee damage by +3 hp (+1.5 hearts) × level. You can find 2 levels:

Level 1-> +3 hp (+1.5 hearts) Melee Damage
Level 2-> +6 hp (+3 hearts) Melee Damage

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Strength Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- All Lingering Potions of Strength cloud lasts 30 seconds at most

- With a beacon set to Strength, your strength effect replenishes when in range. Getting 2 effects at once requires beacon pyramid level 4

- In Being a Zombie Villager, this mob can get the effect when being cured and the difficulty is normal while the level 2 is the same but the difficulty is hard

- The cause of ¨Spawning within the world¨ lasts for 3 years, 4 months, 25 days, 6 hours, 45 minutes, and 42.4 seconds, or (2^31)-1 ticks. Only spiders can have this
.

🤕 Weakness 🤕

1. Description - Weakness decreases attack power. Melee damage inflicted by the affected entity is reduced by -4 hp (-2 hearts) × level. This effect is also used to cure zombie villagers, preceding the golden apple. The effect can be removed by drinking milk. You can find 1 level:

Level 1-> -4 hp (-2 hearts) Melee Damage

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Weakness Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- Witches throw the Splash Potion of Weakness if their target is within 3 blocks

- The Suspicious Stew (Tulip) must be crafted from a tulip. (#food Category 9 to get more information about suspicious stew)

- The Suspicious Stew (Expert Farmer Villagers) is traded from expert farmer villagers. (#villagers Category 4 to get more information about trades)

- The Suspicious Stew of Weakness can be found in shipwreck supply chests
.

❤️ Instant Health ❤️

1. Description - Instant Health is an instant status effect that increases health for living mobs and damages the undead. Instantly heals +4 hp (+2 hearts) × level. When applied using a lingering potion, the entity is healed every second. You can find 2 levels:

Level 1-> +4 hp (+2 hearts). Undead Mobs-> -6 hp (-3 hearts)
Level 2-> +8 hp (+4 hearts). Undead Mobs-> -12 hp (-6 hearts)

❗ IMPORTANT ❗

- Undead mobs (including the wither) are damaged as if with Instant Damage, instead

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Instant Health Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- Witches drink the Potion of Healing when damaged

- The Potion of Healing 1 and 2 can be found on a brewing stand in end ships

- Witches throw Splash Potion of Healing 1 or 2 during raids. (#villagers Category 5 to get more information about raids)

☠️ Instant Damage ☠️

1. Description - Instant Damage is an instant status effect that decreases health for living mobs and heals the undead. Inflicts magic damage of -6 hp (-3 hearts) x level. When applied using a lingering potion, damage is inflicted every second. As this is magic damage, it can be decreased only via Resistance and Protection. You can find 2 levels:

Level 1-> -6 hp (-3 hearts). Undead Mobs-> +6 hp (+3 hearts)
Level 2-> -12 hp (-6 hearts). Undead Mobs-> +12 hp (+6 hearts)

❗ IMPORTANT ❗

- Undead mobs (including the wither) are healed as if with Instant Health instead
- An Instant Damage 4 potion is powerful enough to kill a player instantly

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Instant Damage Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- Remember that damage is for live mobs and heals for undead mobs

- Witches throw the Splash Potion of Harming at their targets

⬆️ Jump Boost ⬆️

1. Description - Jump Boost allows the player to jump higher than the normal +1 1⁄4 blocks. Each level adds +50% to the jump height. It also reduces fall damage by -1 hp (-0.5 heart) each level. You can find 2 levels:

Level 1-> +50% Jump Height. -1 hp (-0.5 heart) Fall Damage Reduction
Level 2-> +100% Jump Height. -2 hp (-1 heart) Fall Damage Reduction

Arbitrary levels can be set via commands

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Jump Boost Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- Jump boost level 1 increases jump height to +1 13⁄16 blocks

- Jump boost level 2 increases jump height to +2 1⁄2 blocks
.

🤢 Nausea 🤢

1. Description - Nausea is an effect that warps and wobbles the player's vision similar to a nether portal. The effect does not change its power as its potency changes. It can be obtained only from eating a pufferfish. Drinking milk removes the effect

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Nausea Causes:

.
💓 Regeneration 💓

1. Description - Regeneration is a status effect that restores a player's (or mob's) health over time. The amount of health healed over time is shown here:

Level 1-> heals 1 hp each 2.5 seconds

Level 2-> heals 1 hp each 1.25 seconds

Level 3-> heals 1 hp each 0.6 seconds

Level 4-> heals 1 hp each 0.3 seconds

Level 5-> heals 1 hp each 0.15 seconds

Level 6-> heals 1 hp each 0.05 seconds

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Regeneration Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- The cause of ¨Spawning within the world¨ lasts for 3 years, 4 months, 25 days, 6 hours, 45 minutes, and 42.4 seconds, or (2^31)-1 ticks. Only spiders can have this

- The unlocking trades only applies to villagers. Regenerates +4 hp (+2 hearts)

- Having low health only applies to Axolotls
.

🛡️ Resistance 🛡️

1. Description - Resistance is a status effect that reduces incoming damage from all sources (except starvation, the void, and /kill) by +20% × level. You can find 4 levels:

Level 1-> +20% Reduction
Level 2-> +40% Reduction
Level 3-> +60% Reduction
Level 4-> +80% Reduction

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Resistance Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- Beacon set to Resistance replenishes your effect when in range and it requires beacon pyramid level 2. The Beacon set to Resistance 2 requires beacon pyramid level 4

🛡️ 🔥 Fire Resistance 🔥 🛡️

1. Description- Fire Resistance nullifies most fire-based damage. Fire Resistance is a status effect that does not change its power as its potency changes. Grants immunity to damage from fire, blaze fireballs, fire charges, magma blocks, and lava, but not ghast fireballs and blaze touch attacks. Negates the fire damage from bows enchanted with Flame and swords enchanted with Fire Aspect, but does not affect the attacks themselves. The fog effect under lava is also mitigated somewhat. Players also see better under lava when they have the Fire Resistance effect

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Fire Resistance Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- Witches drink the Potion of Fire Resistance when set on fire or in lava

- The Suspicious Stew (Allium) must be crafted with Allium

💧 Water Breathing 💧

1. Description - Water Breathing is a status effect that prevents or delays drowning

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Water Breathing Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- Witches drink Potion of Water Breathing when underwater

- In Turtle Shell, the effect only counts down underwater. Instantly replenishes in air

🪞 Invisibility 🪞

1. Description - Invisibility is a status effect that turns entities invisible. It has one potency level (active), but its duration can be extended. Invisibility causes the affected mob to disappear from view although it is still present. Boss mobs are immune to invisibility. Certain features of entities are not affected by invisibility:

- Any armour worn (including horse armour worn by horses)
- Held items
- Any arrows stuck in players ‌[Java Edition only]
- Any particles being emitted
- A shulker head
- A llama's carpet decoration
- A pig's and strider's saddle
- The aura of a charged creeper
- The eyes of cave spiders, spiders, enderman, and phantoms

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Invisibility Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- Wandering Traders drink the Potion of Invisibility if the time is between 12000 and 18000

- Illusioner applies only to illusioners when casting the invisibility spell

- The cause of ¨Spawning within the world¨ lasts for 3 years, 4 months, 25 days, 6 hours, 45 minutes, and 42.4 seconds, or (2^31)-1 ticks. Only spiders can have this

👁️ ❌ Blindness ❌ 👁️

1. Description - Blindness impairs the player's vision as if a thick black fog were surrounding them, with only the immediate area being visible (this means that only a few blocks directly around the player are visible to them). However, the sun and moon can be seen as normal. Additionally, liquids do not fade into the fog perfectly. The effect also prevents the player from sprinting or inflicting critical hits. If combined with Night Vision, the screen appears completely black aside from the sun and moon. In 1.16, combining with night visions renders the HUD text black (this also happens on the title screen)

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Blindness Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- The Suspicious Stew (Azure Bluet) mus be crafted with Azure Bluet

- The Suspicious Stew of Blindness can be found in shipwreck supply chests and traded from expert farmer villagers

🌖 Night Vision 🌖

1. Description - Night vision greatly increases the brightness, so the player can easily see in a light level of 0. However, it is not as bright as a light level of 15 (e.g. with the "Moody" brightness setting, it is similar to sky light level 12–14 with the "Bright" brightness setting), and as such the player can distinguish between light levels

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Night Vision Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- Conduit Power only can be obtained on Bedrock

- The Suspicious Stew (Poppy) must be made with Poppy

- The Suspicious Stew of Night Vision can be found in shipwreck and traded by expert farmers

🍗 Hunger 🍗

1. Description - Hunger increases food exhaustion by -0.005 × level per game tick. It also turns the hunger bar a yellow-green colour. The status effect does not decrease hunger level on Peaceful mode, although it does re-colour the hunger bar. An example of how eating rotten flesh can cause the hunger status effect:

📝 Example 📝

Hunger inflicted by eating rotten flesh, raw chicken or by being attacked by a husk adds +3 to the player's exhaustion level over the course of 30 seconds, draining 3/4 of a saturation point. When a pufferfish is eaten, +4.5 exhaustion points are added over the course of 15 seconds, draining 1 and 1⁄8 (0.125) saturation points

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Hunger Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- In Husk, Regional difficulty or local difficulty is a value between 0.00 and 6.75 that the game calculates by considering not just the world difficulty setting, but also the inhabited time of a chunk, the total daytime in the world, and the phase of the moon. You get this effect by one attack of them

- The Rotten Flesh have 80% chance of receiving. Does not apply to Wolves when fed rotten flesh

- The Raw Chicken have 30% chance of receiving. Does not apply to Wolves when fed raw chicken

☢️ Poison ☢️

1. Description - Poison inflicts damage over time, reducing the player's health to -1 hp (-0.5 heart), but can resume if healing occurs and the effected entity is at more than -1 hp (-0.5 heart) before the effect expires, but cannot kill. It can be received from various mobs and items. It can be cured by drinking milk and honey bottle. The amount of damage inflicted to the affected entity is shown here:

Level 1-> damages 1 hp each 1.25 seconds

Level 2-> damages 1 hp each 0.6 seconds

Level 3-> damages 1 hp each 0.5 seconds

Because of the redphase rules there can't be higher damage values even with higher levels

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Poison Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- Witches throw the Splash Potion of Poison if their target has 8 hp (4 hearts) or more health

- In Cookie, affects only parrots.‌ Has no effect other than the particles as the parrot is killed instantly

- The Poisonous Potato has 60% chance

- The Suspicious Stew (Lily of the Valley) must be crafted from a Lily of the Valley

- The Suspicious Stew (Expert Farmers Villagers) can be traded by expert farmers villagers

- The Spider Eye is dropped from spiders and apply poison when eaten

- The length of the effect given by the cave spider depends the difficulty, as you see in the table, 0:07 seconds (normal difficulty) - 0:15 seconds (hard difficulty) when it attacks an entity

- The length of the effect given by the pufferfish depends how inflated the mob is, partially is 0:03 seconds and fully 0:06 seconds. Only when touched

- The length of the effect given by bee is the same as that of the cave spider, 0:10 seconds on normal difficulty and 0:18 seconds on hard difficulty
.

🖤 Wither 🖤

1. Description - Wither effect is a status effect that inflicts damage over time. Unlike Poison, it can affect undead mobs, and can kill. It is usually difficult for the player to see how much health they have left, as it turns the player's health bar black. The player's hearts turn black on Survival mode or on Hardcore‌ mode, making it more difficult, but still possible, for the player to see their health. The amount of damage inflicted to the affected entity is shown here:

Level 1-> damages 1 hp each 2 seconds

Level 2-> damages 1 hp each 1 seconds

Level 3-> damages 1 hp each 0.5 seconds

Because of the redphase rules there can't be higher damage values even with higher levels

❗ IMPORTANT ❗

- Due to damage immunity, the effective rate is 10 ticks (-2 hp (-1 heart) per second) at levels 4 and up

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Wither Causes:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- The length of the effect and the lifetime damage given by the wither depends the difficulty, as you see in the table: Length - 0:10 seconds (normal difficulty) - 0:40 seconds (hard difficulty) and Lifetime Damage - -10 hp (-5 hearts) (normal difficulty) - -40 hp (-20 hearts) (hard difficulty). When wither skulls make a direct hit on the target, you have wither effect. Normal and Hard difficulty only

- In Wither Skeletons the effect is given melee attack only

- In Wither Rose the effect is given only when in range (within the block)

- The Suspicious Stew (Wither Rose) must be made with Wither Rose

❤️‍🔥 Health Boost ❤️‍🔥

1. Description - Health Boost is an unused status effect that increases a player's (or mob's) maximum health. Adds +4 hp (+2 hearts) maximum health per level. Unlike Absorption, the added hearts are empty at first, but can be healed through the usual methods (such as natural regeneration and the Regeneration and Instant Health effects). When the effect ends, any extra health is lost. Actual health may be above the base value after the effect ends and are not capped, unless the entity is healed. Extra hearts of a mounted mob can be seen while riding it

2. Causes - There are no causes
.

💛 Absorption 💛

1. Description - Absorption is a status effect that pads the health bar with extra hearts. Absorption adds +4 hp (+2 hearts) additional health points per level to the player, displayed as yellow hearts above the normal health bar. If the player takes damage while under this effect, the absorption health points are depleted first, followed by the standard health points. Absorption health cannot be replenished by natural regeneration or other effects, and vanishes when the effect ends. Negative absorption levels do not appear to have an immediate effect when applied, but give +4 hp (+2 hearts) additional health points per level to the player when the status effect ends. You can find 4 levels:

Level 1-> +4 hp (+2 hearts) additional health
Level 2-> +8 hp (+4 hearts) additional health
Level 3-> +12 hp (+6 hearts) additional health
Level 4-> +16 hp (+8 hearts) additional health

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Absorption Causes:

.
💗 Saturation 💗

1. Description - Saturation is an instant status effect that replenishes Hunger and Saturation Points.
The Saturation effect replenishes +2 hunger points (+1 drumstick) × level and +2 × level points of saturation for the first tick. If the effect lasts longer than one tick, the player continues gaining hunger and saturation points +1 hunger point (+0.5 drumstick) and +2 saturation points on each tick.

2. Causes - There are only 1 cause, eating a Suspicious Stew made with a Blue Orchid or Dandelion, the potency is 1 and length 0.35 seconds which is 7 ticks

🔮 Glowing 🔮

1. Description - Glowing causes entities to glow with an outline that can be seen through blocks and entities. This outline is white by default, but can be set to display other colours if the entity is part of a team. The outline displays around any holes in a mob's texture or model, though only when that part of the model can be seen all the way through. If multiple entities with glowing are near each other, the outlines merge to prevent overlapping

❗ IMPORTANT ❗

- This does not affect mob models as seen in the inventory, of either the player or ridden mobs

2. Causes - There are 2 causes:

- Spectral Arrow, potency 1 and length 0:10 seconds

- Bell, potency 1 and length 0:03 seconds (If an illager is within 32 blocks, hitting a bell applies the effect to any illagers within 32 blocks) (#villagers Category 3 to get more information about the variants of villagers)
.

☁️ Levitation ☁️

1. Description - Levitation causes the affected entity to float upwards at a rate of +0.9 × level blocks per second. This does not affect swimming or flying. An affected entity does not take fall damage until the effect wears off, after which the entity falls and takes damage as usual from falling. Levitation has no effect on players riding entities. It also has no effect on entities that are in water or lava

2. Causes -There are 1 cause:

- Shulker, potency 1 and length 0:10 seconds

🍀 Luck 🍀

1. Description - Luck is a status effect that makes it more likely to receive better loot from certain loot tables in generated structures

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Luck Causes:

.
🪶 Slow Falling 🪶

1. Description - Slow Falling is a status effect that causes the affected mob to fall slower and take no fall damage, but does not prevent ender pearl damage. The affected entity falls at a much slower rate than normal, and is immune to fall damage. However, the entity still takes damage from using an ender pearl. In addition, the entity cannot turn farmland into dirt by jumping on it

❗ IMPORTANT ❗

- Higher levels do not decrease fall speed further

2. Causes - Table with the causes:

Slow Falling:

.
🐬 Dolphin´s Grace 🐬

1. Description - Is a status effect that increases the player's swimming speed when a dolphin is nearby and following the player, decreases the amount of "friction" from moving through water. This causes the player to swim significantly faster and lose speed at a slower rate, but also makes changing directions slower. This effect allows you to travel +9.8 blocks/second underwater without Depth Strider, making it faster than a boat. Combining it with Depth Strider, players are able to travel at much higher speeds, adding +8.983 blocks/second x level. Potentially higher speeds are possible by adding Soul Soil underwater and using Soul Speed-enchanted boots, along with Speed 2

❗ IMPORTANT ❗

- Dolphins dont give this effect to players with the Invisibility effect but dolphins do apply the effect to invisible players with any armour piece or headgear equipped

2. Causes - The player must swim near a dolphin to achieve this effect, the potency is random and the length is 0:05 seconds
.

🪓 Bad Omen 🪓

1. Description - Bad Omen is a status effect that causes a raid to appear when an afflicted player enters a village. Bad Omen's potency determines the chance for illagers to be equipped with enchanted weapons when the player triggers a raid by entering a certain radius around a bed that a villager has claimed. If the raid results in player victory, the Hero of the Village's potency equals the Bad Omen's potency (capped at level 5). Bad Omen levels past the first will also give a single extra raid wave, given the difficulty level

📝 Example 📝

Bad Omen 2-5 , Easy will have 4 waves instead of 3, Normal will have 6 waves instead of 5, and Hard will have 8 waves instead of 7

2. Causes - There are 2 causes:

- Raid Captain, potency 1 and length 1:40:00 hours (If the outpost captain is killed by a player or tamed wolf)

- Raid Captain, potency 1-5 and length 1:40:00 hours (If the patrol captain is killed by a player or tamed wolf)
.

💸 Hero Of The Village 💸

1. Description - Hero Of The Village is a status effect granted to the player upon defeating a raid. Players receive gifts (#villagers To see that gifts!)‌ and discounts from villager trades while under the effect. Level 1 Hero of the Village decreases the cost of the first item in a trade by -30%; each additional level decreases the price by an additional -1⁄16 (-6.25%). In Survival, the maximum level is 5, giving discounts of -55% and -30%, respectively. Nevertheless, one can use commands to give higher levels of the effect. Hero of the Village 12 gives a discount of -98.75%, decreasing all prices to 1. No matter how large the discount is, the final item count in the trade is always at least one, never zero. In other cases, the decrement is the discount ratio multiplied by the original count rounded down or rounded up if the decrement is less than 1

📝 Example 📝

Level 3 would give a -42.5% discount. For trade with 14 emeralds as the cost, the discount would be 5 emeralds (rounded down from 5.95 emeralds), for a final price of 9 emeralds

2. Causes - There are 1 cause:

- All illagers in the final wave of a raid are killed, potency 1-5 and length 40 minutes shown as ^^.^^ (The player must have killed at least one raider. The level is the same as the level of Bad Omen the raid was started with)
.

Category 5: 💡 Effects Tips 💡

Here you can see some tips about effects that can help you in some decisions and games:

- Use slow falling arrows or potions to prevent your opponent from doing critical hits

- When the damage lost from weakness is higher than the damage of your weapon, the attacks are completely useless and you can't deal any kind of damage (not even a hit)

- While you have slowness you can still move fast when doing sprint jumps

- With jump boost 2 you can stack yourself up pretty fast (2 blocks per jump)

text: 🧪 Effects 🧪 Author: iDexy Translator: Zivkovic Writer: iDexy In this channel all effects of the game are listed and explained how they influence the player Category 1: 📖 Basic Things 📖 - An effect is a helpful or harmful condition that affects an entity. To use splash potions, throw the potion to the ground to get the effect of the potion. To use lingering potions, throw the potion to the ground or a block to create an effect cloud with the effect of that potion ❗ IMPORTANT ❗ - If you have splash potions, throw the potion up in the air to get the maximum power of the potion (the effect will last longer) - When a creeper has an effect and explodes, it leaves an area effect cloud for each effect that it had before it died - Players can open their inventory to see any current effects afflicted upon them, as well as its level and duration - However, it is not possible to apply the same effect multiple times, even if they are of different levels (e.g. Strength and Strength 2) - Positive effects have blue text in potion information, and in are displayed on the upper row of effects in the heads up display, while negative effects have red potion text and are displayed in the bottom row. Neutral effects have the blue potion text and are listed with the negative effects in the bottom row in the heads up display . Category 2: 🩺 Behaviour 🩺 Basic Things: - Any entities inflicted by an effect are affected in various ways for an amount of time - During the effect, spiral-shaped particles emanate from the position of the inflicted entity - For most effects, higher levels increase the strength of the effect ❗ IMPORTANT ❗ - Note that even with commands, effects cannot be made to last forever. If an effect is set to last a time greater than 32766 (215−2) ticks, 27 minutes and 18 seconds, or 1638 seconds , it displays as ^^.^^ , but still continues ticking down and eventually expires . - Any number of different effects, including opposing effects such as Strength and Weakness, can be simultaneously active on a player - When the stronger effect then overrides the weaker effect, the weaker effect remains, but is hidden. It returns after the stronger effect expires, if the weaker effect has a higher duration than the stronger effect. This change makes it impossible to create custom potion antidotes by applying an amplified effect with a one tick duration - All effects can be removed by drinking milk, dying, being saved from death by a totem of undying, or traveling through the return portal in the End . You can find 4 levels: Level 1-> +4 hp (+2 hearts) additional health Level 2-> +8 hp (+4 hearts) additional health Level 3-> +12 hp (+6 hearts) additional health Level 4-> +16 hp (+8 hearts) additional health 2. Causes - Table with the causes: Absorption Causes: . 💗 Saturation 💗 1. Description - Saturation is an instant status effect that replenishes Hunger and Saturation Points. An affected entity does not take fall damage until the effect wears off, after which the entity falls and takes damage as usual from falling. Levitation has no effect on players riding entities. Description - Luck is a status effect that makes it more likely to receive better loot from certain loot tables in generated structures 2. Causes - Table with the causes: Luck Causes: . 🪶 Slow Falling 🪶 1. Causes - Table with the causes: Slow Falling: . 🐬 Dolphin´s Grace 🐬 1. This causes the player to swim significantly faster and lose speed at a slower rate, but also makes changing directions slower. This effect allows you to travel +9.8 blocks/second underwater without Depth Strider, making it faster than a boat. Combining it with Depth Strider, players are able to travel at much higher speeds, adding +8.983 blocks/second x level . Potentially higher speeds are possible by adding Soul Soil underwater and using Soul Speed-enchanted boots, along with Speed 2 ❗ IMPORTANT ❗ - Dolphins dont give this effect to players with the Invisibility effect but dolphins do apply the effect to invisible players with any armour piece or headgear equipped 2. Causes - The player must swim near a dolphin to achieve this effect, the potency is random and the length is 0:05 seconds . 🪓 Bad Omen 🪓 1. Description - Bad Omen is a status effect that causes a raid to appear when an afflicted player enters a village. Bad Omen's potency determines the chance for illagers to be equipped with enchanted weapons when the player triggers a raid by entering a certain radius around a bed that a villager has claimed. If the raid results in player victory, the Hero of the Village's potency equals the Bad Omen's potency (capped at level 5 ). Bad Omen levels past the first will also give a single extra raid wave, given the difficulty level 📝 Example 📝 Bad Omen 2-5 , Easy will have 4 waves instead of 3 , Normal will have 6 waves instead of 5 , and Hard will have 8 waves instead of 7 2. In this channel all effects of the game are listed and explained how they influence the player

***Category 1:*** 📖 `Basic Things` 📖 

`-` An effect is a helpful or harmful condition that affects an entity. Effects can be inflicted in various ways throughout the game, including consuming potions and some food items, being in the range of beacons and conduits, and being attacked by or close to certain mobs

`-` The `/effect` command allows players to inflict effects upon themselves and other entities

`-` You can get them with Normal potions, splash potions lingering potions and tipped arrows

`-` To use normal potions, you just drink the potion. To use splash potions, throw the potion to the ground to get the effect of the potion. To use lingering potions, throw the potion to the ground or a block to create an effect cloud with the effect of that potion

❗ **__IMPORTANT__** ❗ 

`-` If you have splash potions, throw the potion up in the air to get the maximum power of the potion (the effect will last longer)

`-` When a creeper has an effect and explodes, it leaves an area effect cloud for each effect that it had before it died

`-` Players can open their inventory to see any current effects afflicted upon them, as well as its level and duration

`-` However, it is not possible to apply the same effect multiple times, even if they are of different levels (e.g. Strength and Strength 2)

`-` Positive effects have blue text in potion information, and in are displayed on the upper row of effects in the heads up display, while negative effects have red potion text and are displayed in the bottom row. Neutral effects have the blue potion text and are listed with the negative effects in the bottom row in the heads up display
.

***Category 2:*** 🩺 `Behaviour` 🩺 

**Basic Things:**

`-` Any entities inflicted by an effect are affected in various ways for an amount of time

`-` During the effect, spiral-shaped particles emanate from the position of the inflicted entity

`-` For most effects, higher levels increase the strength of the effect

❗ **__IMPORTANT__** ❗ 

`-` Note that even with commands, effects cannot be made to last forever. If an effect is set to last a time greater than `32766 (215−2) ticks, 27 minutes and 18 seconds, or 1638 seconds`, it displays as `^^.^^`, but still continues ticking down and eventually expires
.

`-` Any number of different effects, including opposing effects such as Strength and Weakness, can be simultaneously active on a player

`-` When the stronger effect then overrides the weaker effect, the weaker effect remains, but is hidden. It returns after the stronger effect expires, if the weaker effect has a higher duration than the stronger effect. This change makes it impossible to create custom potion antidotes by applying an amplified effect with a one tick duration

`-` All effects can be removed by drinking milk, dying, being saved from death by a totem of undying, or traveling through the return portal in the End
.

The affected entity falls at a much slower rate than normal, and is immune to fall damage. However, the entity still takes damage from using an ender pearl. In addition, the entity cannot turn farmland into dirt by jumping on it

❗ **__IMPORTANT__** ❗ 

`-` Higher levels do not decrease fall speed further

`2.` **Causes** - Table with the causes:

**Slow Falling:**

.
🐬 `Dolphin´s Grace` 🐬 

`1.` **Description** - Is a status effect that increases the player's swimming speed when a dolphin is nearby and following the player, decreases the amount of "friction" from moving through water. This causes the player to swim significantly faster and lose speed at a slower rate, but also makes changing directions slower. This effect allows you to travel `+9.8 blocks/second` underwater without Depth Strider, making it faster than a boat. Combining it with Depth Strider, players are able to travel at much higher speeds, adding `+8.983 blocks/second x level`. Potentially higher speeds are possible by adding Soul Soil underwater and using Soul Speed-enchanted boots, along with Speed 2

❗ **__IMPORTANT__** ❗ 

`-` Dolphins dont give this effect to players with the Invisibility effect but dolphins do apply the effect to invisible players with any armour piece or headgear equipped

`2.` **Causes** - The player must swim near a dolphin to achieve this effect, the potency is random and the length is `0:05 seconds`
.

🪓 `Bad Omen` 🪓 

`1.` **Description** - Bad Omen is a status effect that causes a raid to appear when an afflicted player enters a village. Bad Omen's potency determines the chance for illagers to be equipped with enchanted weapons when the player triggers a raid by entering a certain radius around a bed that a villager has claimed. __If the raid results in player victory, the Hero of the Village's potency equals the Bad Omen's potency__ (capped at level `5`). Bad Omen levels past the first will also give a single extra raid wave, given the difficulty level

📝 **__Example__** 📝 

> Bad Omen `2-5` , Easy will have `4` waves instead of `3`, Normal will have `6` waves instead of `5`, and Hard will have `8` waves instead of `7`

`2.` **Causes** - There are `2` causes:

`-` Raid Captain, potency `1` and length `1:40:00 hours` (If the outpost captain is killed by a player or tamed wolf)

`-` Raid Captain, potency `1-5` and length `1:40:00 hours` (If the patrol captain is killed by a player or tamed wolf)
.

💸 `Hero Of The Village` 💸 

`1.` **Description** - Hero Of The Village is a status effect granted to the player upon defeating a raid. Players receive gifts (<#852244533705965599> To see that gifts!)‌ and discounts from villager trades while under the effect. Level `1` Hero of the Village decreases the cost of the first item in a trade by `-30%`; each additional level decreases the price by an additional `-1⁄16 (-6.25%)`. __In Survival, the maximum level is `5`__, giving discounts of `-55%` and `-30%`, respectively. Nevertheless, one can use commands to give higher levels of the effect. Hero of the Village `12` gives a discount of `-98.75%`, decreasing all prices to `1`. No matter how large the discount is, the final item count in the trade is always at least one, never zero. In other cases, the decrement is the discount ratio multiplied by the original count rounded down or rounded up if the decrement is less than `1`

📝 **__Example__** 📝 

> Level `3` would give a `-42.5%` discount. For trade with `14` emeralds as the cost, the discount would be `5` emeralds (rounded down from `5.95` emeralds), for a final price of `9` emeralds

`2.` **Causes** - There are `1` cause:

`-` All illagers in the final wave of a raid are killed, potency `1-5` and length `40 minutes` shown as `^^.^^` (The player must have killed at least one raider. The level is the same as the level of Bad Omen the raid was started with)
.

***Category 5:*** 💡 `Effects Tips` 💡 

Here you can see some tips about effects that can help you in some decisions and games:

`-` Use slow falling arrows or potions to prevent your opponent from doing critical hits

`-` When the damage lost from weakness is higher than the damage of your weapon,  the attacks are completely useless and you can't deal any kind of damage (not even a hit)

`-` While you have slowness you can still move fast when doing sprint jumps

`-` With jump boost 2 you can stack yourself up pretty fast (2 blocks per jump)

`-` Use instant damage pots or arrows against unenchanted or low level enchanted armour as a surprise attack to finish your opponent quickly

`-` Poison can be used to prevent opponents from running away because they are slowed every time it damages them
.

`-` Because of the bonus or deduction of armour penetration from strength and weakness, they are an even stronger influence

`-` When you're poisoned or burning, time your jump so that the damage happens when you're on the ground to do critical hits

`-` When you eat an enchanted golden apple first, normal golden apples don't give the absorption effect as long the absorption of the enchanted golden apple is active

`-` Use tipped arrows to shoot yourself in long fights to gain effects like speed and strength , you can carry 64 in one slot while you can only carry one potion in a slot

🧪 ***__Effects__*** 🧪

**Author:** `iDexy`
**Translator:** `Zivkovic`
**Writer:** `iDexy`

In this channel all effects of the game are listed and explained how they influence the player

***Category 1:*** 📖 `Basic Things` 📖 

`-` An effect is a helpful or harmful condition that affects an entity. Effects can be inflicted in various ways throughout the game, including consuming potions and some food items, being in the range of beacons and conduits, and being attacked by or close to certain mobs

`-` The `/effect` command allows players to inflict effects upon themselves and other entities

`-` You can get them with Normal potions, splash potions lingering potions and tipped arrows

`-` To use normal potions, you just drink the potion. To use splash potions, throw the potion to the ground to get the effect of the potion. To use lingering potions, throw the potion to the ground or a block to create an effect cloud with the effect of that potion

❗ **__IMPORTANT__** ❗ 

`-` If you have splash potions, throw the potion up in the air to get the maximum power of the potion (the effect will last longer)

`-` When a creeper has an effect and explodes, it leaves an area effect cloud for each effect that it had before it died

`-` Players can open their inventory to see any current effects afflicted upon them, as well as its level and duration

`-` However, it is not possible to apply the same effect multiple times, even if they are of different levels (e.g. Strength and Strength 2)

`-` Positive effects have blue text in potion information, and in are displayed on the upper row of effects in the heads up display, while negative effects have red potion text and are displayed in the bottom row. Neutral effects have the blue potion text and are listed with the negative effects in the bottom row in the heads up display
.

messages.author: iDexy
messages.sourceText:
***Category 2:*** 🩺 `Behaviour` 🩺 

**Basic Things:**

`-` Any entities inflicted by an effect are affected in various ways for an amount of time

`-` During the effect, spiral-shaped particles emanate from the position of the inflicted entity

`-` For most effects, higher levels increase the strength of the effect

❗ **__IMPORTANT__** ❗ 

`-` Note that even with commands, effects cannot be made to last forever. If an effect is set to last a time greater than `32766 (215−2) ticks, 27 minutes and 18 seconds, or 1638 seconds`, it displays as `^^.^^`, but still continues ticking down and eventually expires
.

messages.author: iDexy
messages.sourceText:
`-` Any number of different effects, including opposing effects such as Strength and Weakness, can be simultaneously active on a player

`-` When the stronger effect then overrides the weaker effect, the weaker effect remains, but is hidden. It returns after the stronger effect expires, if the weaker effect has a higher duration than the stronger effect. This change makes it impossible to create custom potion antidotes by applying an amplified effect with a one tick duration

`-` All effects can be removed by drinking milk, dying, being saved from death by a totem of undying, or traveling through the return portal in the End
.

__Let's follow the order of the summary effects:__

🥾 `Speed` 🥾 

`1.` **Description** - Speed is a status effect that increases an entity's walking speed by `+20%` multiplied by the effect level. It expands a player's field of view (`FOV`) accordingly. You can find `2` levels:

**Level 1->** `+20%` Speed
**Level 2->** `+40%` Speed

❗ **__IMPORTANT__** ❗

`-` Your FOV increases when you have speed effect but you can disable in the accessibility settings

`-` With a beacon set to Speed, your speed effect replenishes when in range. Getting 2 effects at once requires beacon pyramid level 4

🐢 `Slowness` 🐢 

`1.` **Description** - Slowness decreases walking speed by `-15% × level` and contracts the player's field of view accordingly. Negative levels of Slowness increase walking speed. However, sprinting and jumping is barely affected. You can find `6` levels:

**Level 1->** `-15%` Walking Speed
**Level 2->** `-30%` Walking Speed
**Level 3->** `-45%` Walking Speed

`-` The Arrows of Slowness (extended) are fired by Strays

⛏️ `Haste` ⛏️ 

`1.` **Description** - Haste is a status effect that increases attack speed by `+10% x level` and increases mining speed by `+20% x level`. Negative levels decrease mining and attack speed, similar to Mining Fatigue. However, the attack speed increases are purely visual. You can find `2` levels:

**Level 1->** `+10%` Attack Speed. `+20%` Mining Speed
**Level 2->** `+20%` Attack Speed. `+40%` Mining Speed

❗ **__IMPORTANT__** ❗ 

`-` Keep in mind that Mining Fatigue `3` inflicted by elder guardians prevents the player from instant mining most blocks regardless of the Haste effect, along with a huge decrease of mining speed. However, lower levels of Mining Fatigue can be overcome by Haste of level III or greater, with a resultant reduced Haste effect

`2.` **Causes** -  Table with the causes:

🗒️ **__Table Notes__** 🗒️ 

`-` With a beacon set to Haste, your haste effect replenishes when in range. Getting `2` effects at once requires beacon pyramid level `4`

🥄 `Mining Fatigue` 🥄 

`1.` **Description** - The effect decreases attack speed by `-10% × level`, equivalent to the attack speed cooldown attribute decreasing by `-0.2 × level`. For the in-game default level 3, attack speed decreases by `-30%` (attack speed cooldown attribute decreases by `-0.6`), and it takes `~370` times longer than usual to break a block with the proper tool for that block. It decreases also the mining speed. You can find `4` levels:

**Level 1->** `-10%` Attack Speed. `-70%` Mining Speed
**Level 2->** `-20%` Attack Speed. `-91%` Mining Speed 
**Level 3->** `-30%` Attack Speed. `-99.73%` Mining Speed
**Level 4->** `-40%` Attack Speed. `-99.919%` Mining Speed

While afflicted, a player can still craft and ride entities as usual, but cannot remove most vehicles due to how slowly the vehicle can be broken

The affliction is cured by drinking milk, although milk does not prevent a subsequent affliction by an elder guardian, which can happen within a few seconds. Axolotls can also remove this effect

`2.` **Causes** - The only natural cause of Mining Fatigue is from affliction by an elder guardian, and the only natural effect level is `3`. __Other levels can be achieved via commands__

Once per minute, elder guardians in the vicinity search for any player within `50` blocks to afflict with Mining Fatigue `3`. A player cannot defend from this attack. Concealment behind blocks, underground, or by a potion of Invisibility offers no defense. The length of this effect is `5:00 minutes`
.

❤️ `Instant Health` ❤️ 

`1.` **Description** -  Instant Health is an instant status effect that increases health for living mobs and damages the undead. Instantly heals `+4 hp (+2 hearts) × level`. When applied using a lingering potion, the entity is healed every second. You can find `2` levels:

`1.` **Description** - Instant Damage is an instant status effect that decreases health for living mobs and heals the undead. Inflicts magic damage of `-6 hp (-3 hearts) x level`. When applied using a lingering potion, damage is inflicted every second. As this is magic damage, **it can be decreased only via Resistance and Protection**. You can find `2` levels:

`1.` **Description** -  Resistance is a status effect that reduces incoming damage from all sources (except starvation, the void, and `/kill`) by `+20% × level`. You can find `4` levels:

🛡️ 🔥 `Fire Resistance` 🔥 🛡️ 

`1.` **Description**- Fire Resistance nullifies most fire-based damage. Fire Resistance is a status effect that does not change its power as its potency changes. Grants immunity to damage from fire, blaze fireballs, fire charges, magma blocks, and lava, but not ghast fireballs and blaze touch attacks. Negates the fire damage from bows enchanted with Flame and swords enchanted with Fire Aspect, but does not affect the attacks themselves. The fog effect under lava is also mitigated somewhat. Players also see better under lava when they have the Fire Resistance effect

🪞 `Invisibility` 🪞 

`1.` **Description** - Invisibility is a status effect that turns entities invisible. It has one potency level (active), but its duration can be extended. Invisibility causes the affected mob to disappear from view although it is still present. Boss mobs are immune to invisibility. Certain features of entities are not affected by invisibility:

`-` Any armour worn (including horse armour worn by horses)
`-` Held items
`-` Any arrows stuck in players ‌[Java Edition only]
`-` Any particles being emitted
`-` A shulker head
`-` A llama's carpet decoration

👁️ ❌ `Blindness` ❌ 👁️ 

`1.` **Description** - Blindness impairs the player's vision as if a thick black fog were surrounding them, with only the immediate area being visible (this means that only a few blocks directly around the player are visible to them). However, the sun and moon can be seen as normal. **Additionally, liquids do not fade into the fog perfectly**. The effect also prevents the player from sprinting or inflicting critical hits. If combined with Night Vision, the screen appears completely black aside from the sun and moon. In `1.16`, combining with night visions renders the HUD text black (this also happens on the title screen)

🌖 `Night Vision` 🌖 

`1.` **Description** -  Night vision greatly increases the brightness, so the player can easily see in a light level of `0`. However, it is not as bright as a light level of `15` (e.g. with the "Moody" brightness setting, it is similar to sky light level `12–14` with the "Bright" brightness setting), and as such the player can distinguish between light levels

🍗 `Hunger` 🍗 

`1.` **Description** - Hunger increases food exhaustion by `-0.005 × level per game tick`. It also turns the hunger bar a yellow-green colour.  The status effect does not decrease hunger level on Peaceful mode, although it does re-colour the hunger bar. An example of how eating rotten flesh can cause the hunger status effect:

📝 **__Example__** 📝 

> Hunger inflicted by eating rotten flesh, raw chicken or by being attacked by a husk adds `+3` to the player's exhaustion level over the course of `30 seconds`, draining `3/4` of a saturation point. When a pufferfish is eaten, `+4.5` exhaustion points are added over the course of `15 seconds`, draining `1` and `1⁄8 (0.125)` saturation points

`2.` **Causes** - Table with the causes:

**Hunger Causes:**

`-` In Husk, **Regional difficulty or local difficulty** is a value between `0.00` and `6.75` that the game calculates by considering not just the world difficulty setting, but also the inhabited time of a chunk, the total daytime in the world, and the phase of the moon. You get this effect by one attack of them

`-` The Rotten Flesh have `80%` chance of receiving. Does not apply to Wolves when fed rotten flesh

`-` The Raw Chicken have `30%` chance of receiving. Does not apply to Wolves when fed raw chicken

☢️ `Poison` ☢️ 

`1.` **Description** - Poison inflicts damage over time, reducing the player's health to `-1 hp (-0.5 heart)`, but can resume if healing occurs and the effected entity is at more than `-1 hp (-0.5 heart)` before the effect expires, but __cannot kill__. It can be received from various mobs and items. It can be cured by drinking milk and honey bottle. The amount of damage inflicted to the affected entity is shown here:

**Level 1->** `damages 1 hp each 1.25 seconds`

**Level 2->** `damages 1 hp each 0.6 seconds`

**Level 3->** `damages 1 hp each 0.5 seconds`

🍖 Food 🍖

Author: LoCr and iDexy
Translator: Zivkovic
Writer: iDexy

In this channel will we will talk about the food system which controls the regeneration system of minecraft

Category 1: 📖 Basic Things 📖

- As you know, food are consumable items that restore hunger points and sometimes cause status effects

- Its essential for the survival of the player

- Most foods are eaten by holding down "Use Item" except the cake, that must be placed like any other block, before it can be eaten

- A player in survival mode must eat regularly or he will start to lose health until he dies

- Except for the golden apple, Honey jar and milk, the food cannot be eaten when the hunger bar is completely full

- Except for milk, pie, and mushroom stew, food and ingredients can be stacked in inventory

- All types of food are renewable resources (including golden food, since zombified piglin drop gold nuggets and ingots)
.

Category 2: 👨‍🍳 Hunger 👨‍🍳

Hunger is a player-specific feature of Minecraft that regulates player's certain abilities (health regeneration and the ability to sprint) the value of which is managed by the player's activity

Basic things:

- The player's hunger value is shown on the heads-up display in the form of a hunger bar (also called food bar), which is similar to health bar (located above the hotbar), located opposite to it and represented by ten drumsticks (🍗 )

- One half of a drumstick represents one hunger point or half-unit of hunger, cuz the full bar consists of twenty hunger points. like we said in #436138841493995531. It is replenished by eating food, and decreased by player's actions such as sprinting, digging or attacking (We will see this in next categories)

- Various levels of player's hunger control health regeneration (or depletion) and the ability to sprint

- If the hunger bar is at zero, the player's health depletes

- The specific effects are described in next categories

- The hunger value does not drain on Peaceful difficulty and regenerates if it is not at the maximum value

- The hunger indicator is shown above the hotbar, to the other side of the health bar
.

Category 3: 💗 Saturation 💗

An important aspect of hunger not shown on the hunger bar is called food saturation. Its like an invisible extra hunger bar which get filled by eating food too. It also have a maximum of 20 Points and only when it is fully decreased the visible hunger bar will start decreasing. So you can imagine it like an buffer to not constantly losing hunger points. It plays an important role in regenerating the players health. At category 10 will be explained how you can use this system for your advantage in fights

❗ IMPORTANT ❗

- Saturation in 1.12 is different from 1.9
.

Category 4: 🗳️ Hunger and Saturation System 🗳️

The hunger and saturation system is controlled by the variables which are listed below.

1. foodLevel - The player's current hunger level, shown visually on the hunger bar. Its initial value on world creation or respawn is 20 hunger points (10 drumsticks)

2. foodSaturationLevel - The player's current saturation level, which determines how fast the hunger level depletes and is controlled by the kinds of food the player eats. Its maximum value always equals foodLevel's value and decreases with the hunger level. Its initial value on world creation or respawn is 5. Its maximum is 20.

3. foodExhaustionLevel - The player's current exhaustion level, which determines how fast the saturation and hunger points decrease. This value is increased by the player's actions. The initial value is zero. When it reaches the maximum value of 4, it resets to zero and one point is subtracted from the foodSaturationLevel, or when saturation is gone then the foodLevel.

The units of foodLevel are hunger points, the units of foodSaturationLevel are saturation points, and the foodExhaustionLevel is the system to control the decrease of hunger and Saturation points.
The foodExhaustionLevel is controlled by actions you do ingame.

You can imagine the system as a clock where saturation points are minutes and food Exhaustion is seconds. When enough Exhaustion points are gone one saturation point will be removed. If the Saturation is gone, food Exhaustion will remove hunger points. And when you reach zero hunger Points the time runs out and you lose health Points due to starvation damage, until you fill it again with food
.

📝 Example 📝

If a golden carrot (giving 6 hunger points (3 drumsticks) and 14.4 saturation points) is eaten by a player whose hunger bar is at 9 (4.5 drumsticks) and saturation is below 1, its value increases to 15, and the golden carrot's saturation potential is fully used. However, if the hunger level is 8, its value increases to 14 and only 14 saturation points are used
.

Category 5: 😋 Effects of Hunger 😋

Various hunger levels lead to various effects on the player:

1. When the hunger bar is at 20 (10 drumsticks) and there is any saturation left, health regenerates 1 heart every 1⁄2 second

2. When the hunger bar is at 18 (9 drumsticks) or more, health slowly regenerates 1 heart every 4 seconds

3. When hunger is over 17 (8.5 drumsticks), the player's health regenerates. If it falls to 6 (drumsticks), the player loses the ability to sprint

4. If the hunger bar is at 6 (3 drumsticks) points or below, then the player cannot sprint

5. When the hunger bar is at 0, the player's health depletes at a rate of 1 heart every 4 seconds (this makes sleeping impossible). On Easy difficulty, the player's health stops dropping at 10 hearts, on Normal, it stops at 1 heart, and on Hard, it keeps draining until either the player eats something or starves to death. Resistance and armour do not reduce starvation damage

Switching to Peaceful difficulty eliminates all penalties above, and rapidly restores the player's hunger bar and health
.

Category 6: 🔺 Exhaustion Level Increase 🔺

Exhaustion Level Increase remove saturation and food points, this happens with actions like sprinting, getting hit, or attacking. Any action not listed in the table does not increase exhaustion level. For example, normal walking doesn't increase exhaustion, and therefore does not decrease saturation or the food bar

Exhaustion Table:

.

Category 7: 🥩 Food Information 🥩

In this category you can see a excel table of food information. In this excel table you can see things like food points, saturation restored, effective quality and saturation ratio:

Alphabetical Order

Food Table:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- Keep in mind that 1 food point is half a "drumstick" or hunger point. So if a food has 12 food points, it will have 6 hunger points. Just divide the food points by 2 to get the hunger points

- How i can calculate the saturation ratio and effective quality? - The saturation ratio can be calculated with this formula: food points ÷ saturation restored. The effective quality can be calculated with this formula: food points + saturation restored

- In the table we can extract the food with the best food points, saturation restored, effective quality, saturation ratio and the best food comparing this 4 things:

Highest Food Points - Cake Whole
Highest Saturation Restored - Suspicious Stew (Saturation)
Highest Effective Quality - Suspicious Stew (Saturation)
Highest Saturation Ratio - Enchanted Golden Apple, Golden Apple and Golden Carrot
Best Food Comparing this 4 things - Suspicious Stew (Saturation)
.

Category 8: 🧪 Food Effects/Special Properties 🦠

Some foods give potion effects or have special properties. There are 12 of them. Here you can see the foods and their effects/special properties:

(#effects Category 4 to get more information about the effects)

🧪 Effects: 🧪 We can split it in Positive Effects and Negative Effects

Positive Effects:

Alphabetical Order

1. Enchanted Golden Apple - Regeneration II for 20 seconds‌, absorption IV for 2 minutes, resistance for 5 minutes and fire Resistance for 5 minutes

2. Golden Apple - Regeneration II for 5 seconds and absorption for 2 minutes

3. Suspicious Stew - The following for 3-11 seconds, depending on the flower used: (we will talk more about this food in Suspicious Stew Category)

- Regeneration
- Jump Boost
- Poison
- Wither
- Weakness
- Blindness
- Fire Resistance
- Saturation
- Night Vision

.
Negative Effects:

1. Poisonous Potato - Poison for 5 seconds (60% chance)

2. Pufferfish - Hunger III for 15 seconds, nausea for 15 seconds and Poison II for 60 seconds

3. Raw Chicken - Hunger for 30 seconds (30% chance)

4. Rotten Flesh - Hunger for 30 seconds (80% chance)

5. Spider Eye - Poison for 5 seconds

🦠 Special Properties: 🦠

1. Chorus Fruit - The player may be teleported randomly anywhere within 8 blocks of you

2. Honey Bottle - Clears Poison

3. Kelp - Can be eaten faster than other foods twice as fast

4. Milk - You can clear positive/negative effects with the milk. You can use the milk if you have negative effects

Category 9: 🍲 Suspicious Stew 🍲

In this category we will go over all everything you need to know about suspicious stews. We will talk about 3 points:

1. Description - Suspicious stew is a food item that can give the player a status effect, depending on the flower used to craft it

2. Obtaining - Suspicious stew is the only food item in the game that cannot be obtained from the Creative inventory, however it can be crafted and found in shipwreck chests. Here you can see the recipe:

Recipe:

.
Ways to be obtained:

- You can obtain the suspicious stew in chests of a shipwreck. Those stews grants one of the following effects: 5–7 seconds of Blindness, 7–10 seconds of Jump Boost, 7-10 seconds of Night Vision, 10–20 seconds of Poison, 0.3-0.35 seconds of Saturation, or 6–8 seconds of Weakness

- After being given a flower, a brown mushroom cow can be "milked" for suspicious stews by using a bowl on it. The flower type determines the stew's effect using the same rule as a crafted stew. Red mushroom cows cannot be fed flowers or milked for suspicious stew.

- Expert-level farmer villagers can sell 1 or 2 suspicious stew for one emerald

❗ IMPORTANT ❗

- The trading interface does not indicate the type of suspicious stew being sold, but each trade entry will consistently yield the same type of stew, so the player can remember or make a note of the types offered by a given villager, e.g."this villager's first stew gives blindness, and their second entry gives saturation

3. Usage - Eating one suspicious stew restores 6 hunger points (3 food points/drumsticks) and 7.2 saturation points and gives a few seconds of a status effect that varies depending on which flower was used to craft it. Here is a table of flowers and the effects they give when put into a suspicious stew:

.
🗒️ Table Notes 🗒️

- Allium effect duration: 4 seconds

- Azure Bluet effect duration: 8 seconds

- Blue Orchid/Dandelion effect duration: 0.35 seconds

- Cornflower effect duration: 6 seconds

- Lily of the Valley effect duration: 12 seconds

- Oxeye Daisy effect duration: 8 seconds (restore up to 3 hp due regeneration effect)

- Poppy effect duration: 5 seconds

- Tulips effect duration: 9 seconds

- Whiter Rose effect duration: 8 seconds

- Using a suspicious stew with the effect of blindness and saturation is the only way to obtain it in Vanilla Minecraft without the use of commands

- The Saturation effect effectively makes this stew to a super food: In those 6 or 7 ticks it can restore up to 6(7) hunger and 12(14) saturation points on top of their food value, for a total of at least 12 hunger points (6 drumsticks/food points) and effectively maxing out saturation. This is the most amount of hunger and saturation the player can get from a single food item
.

Category 10: 🛡️ 🍗 Saturation Shield 🍗 🛡️

The saturation healing mechanic is pretty important in fights. Its like an invisible set of bonus hearts which will replace your current health points when you get hurt

Because of this, it can be seen as an invisible shield that prevents damage

.
How much does saturation heal the player?

With 20 saturation points the shield is full. Take a look at the table in the saturation chapter to see how much you need to eat to get a full shield. A full shield can heal 13 hp (6.5 hearts) + 2 hp from the hunger bar (1 full heart) so overall you get an extra 15 health points

The speed of the regeneration from saturation is 2 hp (1 heart) per second. When you run out of saturation, you will gain an extra 2 hp (1 heart) from the hunger points over the course of 8 seconds

📜 Special Rule 📜

When you have an amount of saturation with a decimal, the saturation will get rounded up in the final calculation, meaning if you have 12.2 saturation it is 13 saturation

There are different methods to use this “saturation shield” to your advantage:

- First of all the pretty basic one, try to always eat right before a fight so you have a charged "shield" and when it comes to hit trades, you have a better chance of winning because of your fuller shield

- Try to avoid doing many actions that cost saturation (like sprinting) shortly before a fight begins. Because otherwise your saturation will be used for these actions and not for healing. For example, if you only move without sprinting you don't lose any saturation points, and if a fight can't be avoided anyway its better to let them attack you and save your saturation for the fight instead of running

- if your saturation shield is almost empty and only a few saturation points are remaining, to recharge it faster you can quickly hit yourself with fire or arrows to remove the remaining points so your hunger goes down and you can reload it with some more food. You can also build a 2 block high ceiling to sprint jump under it to remove the saturation

.
- Double gap technique, when you eat two golden apples in a row you will gain a full Saturation shield (one golden apple gives 9.6 Saturation, 2 give 19.2 and because of the rule mentioned earlier it will get rounded up to 20)

Because of the full saturation shield you can surprise opponents with it and gain the upper hand in hit trades. Its also pretty good when fighting teams to give you a short health advantage so you can hunt one of them down even if they have the same equipment. Try to eat without being seen

Here are the raw statistics:

One gap: 4 absorption; 4 hp regeneration 9 hp saturation shield --> overall health points: 17 hp (8.5 hearts)
Double gap: 4 hp absorption; 6 hp regeneration; 15 hp saturation shield --> overall health points: 25 hp (12.5 hearts)

The usage of “double gap” has a worse overall efficiency, because you throw away the regeneration and absorption of the second golden apple, but having a full saturation shield outweighs this cost in most cases

Also, sometimes when you have already taken damage, a triple gap could be useful to fill your hearts with the first golden apple and restore your shield with the other two

Other methods to gain a full Saturation shield:

In some cases you can let your food become empty enough (-9 hunger points) and eat two steaks or other high saturation food in a row

You can also eat a suspicious stew which gives the saturation effect

❗ IMPORTANT ❗

Damage overwhelming:

In some low equipment fights where fights are short, the speed of the healing (2 hp (1 heart) each second) could be too slow to shield you. This will be referred to as “damage overwhelming”. When you have a saturation advantage (like you ate more recently than your opponent) try to take as much time with defensive actions to fully convert your saturation to health BUT stay close enough to your opponent so they can’t eat without getting punished. If you have the disadvantage in saturation, try to kill your opponent as fast as you can so they can’t use their advantage

Counter to the shield:

As stupid as it sounds, click spamming is the most efficient way to remove an opponents saturation shield. You will do less damage but since you do it fast and because of how the rounding and counting of saturation works, this will remove their saturation shield fast, even faster than critting them out. But be careful, if the opponent has absorption remaining from a golden apple, you need to deplete the absorption with fully charged hits first because absorption will prevent the saturation from being used

This can be used mainly in highly armoured fights, where armour breaking and damage overwhelming don’t play a big role, while in common scenarios its always better to just hit away the shield with normal and critical hits. Knowing about the spamclick technique will help you know if your shield got drained if someone has been spamclicking you
.

Category 11: 💡 Food Tips 💡

Here you can see some tips about food that can help you in some decisions and games:

- To get the most out of your food you need to eat "slowly"( you need to wait until the regen from the food eaten is over before eating again)

📝 Example 📝

If you eat one carrot it will heal 5 hp (2.5 hearts). If you eat two carrots fast they will heal 7 hp (3.5 hearts). If you eat the carrots, "slowly" you can heal 10 hp (5 hearts) with both carrots

- The best foods are enchanted golden apple, golden apple,suspicious stew (saturation), golden carrots and steak. So try to always use them in your games. You can’t craft enchanted golden apples in versions 1.9+ Keep this in mind

- Honey is good to remove poison and milk clears all effects

- The suspicious stew works like a personal food potion, you can craft a suspicious stew with any effect you want using the correct flower. The speed of the regeneration from saturation is `2 hp (1 heart) per second`. When you run out of saturation, you will gain an extra `2 hp (1 heart)` from the hunger points over the course of `8 seconds`

📜 ***__Special Rule__*** 📜 

When you have an amount of saturation with a decimal, the saturation will get rounded up in the final calculation, meaning if you have `12.2 saturation it is 13 saturation`

There are different methods to use this “saturation shield” to your advantage:

`-` First of all the pretty basic one, try to always eat right before a fight so you have a charged "shield" and when it comes to hit trades, you have a better chance of winning because of your fuller shield 

`-` Try to avoid doing many actions that cost saturation (like sprinting) shortly before a fight begins. Because otherwise your saturation will be used for these actions and not for healing. For example, if you only move without sprinting you don't lose any saturation points, and if a fight can't be avoided anyway its better to let them attack you and save your saturation for the fight instead of running

`-` if your saturation shield is almost empty and only a few saturation points are remaining, to recharge it faster you can quickly hit yourself with fire or arrows to remove the remaining points so your hunger goes down and you can reload it with some more food. You can also build a 2 block high ceiling to sprint jump under it to remove the saturation

.
`-` Double gap technique, when you eat two golden apples in a row you will gain a full Saturation shield (one golden apple gives `9.6 Saturation, 2 give 19.2 and because of the rule mentioned earlier it will get rounded up to 20`)

Because of the full saturation shield you can surprise opponents with it and gain the upper hand in hit trades. Its also pretty good when fighting teams to give you a short health advantage so you can hunt one of them down even if they have the same equipment. Try to eat without being seen

**One gap:** `4 absorption; 4 hp regeneration 9 hp saturation shield` --> overall health points: `17 hp (8.5 hearts)`
**Double gap:** `4 hp absorption; 6 hp regeneration; 15 hp saturation shield` --> overall health points: `25 hp (12.5 hearts)`

The usage of **“double gap”** has a worse overall efficiency, because you throw away the regeneration and absorption of the second golden apple, but having a full saturation shield outweighs this cost in most cases

Also, sometimes when you have already taken damage, a triple gap could be useful to fill your hearts with the first golden apple and restore your shield with the other two

**Other methods to gain a full Saturation shield:**

In some cases you can let your food become empty enough (`-9 hunger points`) and eat two steaks or other high saturation food in a row

You can also eat a suspicious stew which gives the saturation effect

`Damage overwhelming:`

In some low equipment fights where fights are short, the speed of the healing (`2 hp (1 heart)` each second) could be too slow to shield you. This will be referred to as “damage overwhelming”. When you have a saturation advantage (like you ate more recently than your opponent) try to take as much time with defensive actions to fully convert your saturation to health **BUT** stay close enough to your opponent so they can’t eat without getting punished. If you have the disadvantage in saturation, try to kill your opponent as fast as you can so they can’t use their advantage

`Counter to the shield:`

As stupid as it sounds, click spamming is the most efficient way to remove an opponents saturation shield. You will do less damage but since you do it fast and because of how the rounding and counting of saturation works, this will remove their saturation shield fast, even faster than critting them out. But be careful, if the opponent has absorption remaining from a golden apple, you need to deplete the absorption with fully charged hits first because absorption will prevent the saturation from being used

**This can be used mainly in highly armoured fights, where armour breaking and damage overwhelming don’t play a big role, while in common scenarios its always better to just hit away the shield with normal and critical hits. Knowing about the spamclick technique will help you know if your shield got drained if someone has been spamclicking you**
.

Hunger is a player-specific feature of Minecraft that regulates player's certain abilities (health regeneration and the ability to sprint) the value of which is managed by the player's activity

**Basic things:**

`-` The player's hunger value is shown on the heads-up display in the form of a hunger bar (also called food bar), which is similar to health bar (located above the hotbar), located opposite to it and represented by ten drumsticks (🍗 )

`-` __One half of a drumstick represents one hunger point or half-unit of hunger__, cuz the full bar consists of twenty hunger points. **like we said in <#436138841493995531>.** It is replenished by eating food, and decreased by player's actions such as sprinting, digging or attacking **(We will see this in next categories)**

`-` Various levels of player's hunger control health regeneration (or depletion) and the ability to sprint

`-` If the hunger bar is at zero, the player's health depletes

`-` The specific effects are described in **next categories**

`-` The hunger value does not drain on Peaceful difficulty and regenerates if it is not at the maximum value

`-` The hunger indicator is shown above the hotbar, to the other side of the health bar
.

An important aspect of hunger not shown on the hunger bar is called food saturation. Its like an invisible extra hunger bar which get filled by eating food too. It also have a maximum of 20 Points and only when it is fully decreased the visible hunger bar will start decreasing. So you can imagine it like an buffer to not constantly losing hunger points. ❗ **__IMPORTANT__** ❗

.

***Category 4:*** 🗳️ `Hunger and Saturation System` 🗳️ 

The hunger and saturation system is controlled by the variables which are listed below.

`1.` **foodLevel** - The player's current hunger level, shown visually on the hunger bar. Its initial value on world creation or respawn is 20 hunger points (10 drumsticks)

`2.` **foodSaturationLevel** - The player's current saturation level, which determines how fast the hunger level depletes and is controlled by the kinds of food the player eats. Its maximum value always equals foodLevel's value and decreases with the hunger level. Its initial value on world creation or respawn is 5. Its maximum is 20. 

`3.` **foodExhaustionLevel** - The player's current exhaustion level, which determines how fast the saturation and hunger points decrease. This value is increased by the player's actions. The initial value is zero. When it reaches the maximum value of 4, it resets to zero and one point is subtracted from the foodSaturationLevel, or when saturation is gone then the foodLevel. 

The units of foodLevel are hunger points, the units of foodSaturationLevel are saturation points, and the foodExhaustionLevel is the system to control the  decrease of hunger and Saturation points.
The foodExhaustionLevel is controlled by actions you do ingame.

You can imagine the system as a clock where saturation points are minutes and food Exhaustion is seconds. When enough Exhaustion points are gone one saturation point will be removed. If the Saturation is gone, food Exhaustion will remove hunger points. And when you reach zero hunger Points the time runs out and you lose health Points due to starvation damage, until you fill it again with food
.

However, if the hunger level is `8`, its value increases to `14` and only `14` saturation points are used
.

messages.author: iDexy
