***Category 5:*** 😋 `Effects of Hunger` 😋 

Various hunger levels lead to various effects on the player:

`1.` When the hunger bar is at `20 (10 drumsticks)` and there is any saturation left, health regenerates `1 heart` every `1⁄2 second`

`2.` When the hunger bar is at `18 (9 drumsticks)` or more, health slowly regenerates 1 heart every `4 seconds`

`3.` When hunger is over `17 (8.5 drumsticks)`, the player's health regenerates. If it falls to `6 (drumsticks)`, the player loses the ability to sprint

`4.` If the hunger bar is at `6 (3 drumsticks)` points or below, then the player cannot sprint

`5.` When the hunger bar is at `0`, the player's health depletes at a rate of `1 heart` every `4 seconds` (this makes sleeping impossible). On **Easy difficulty**, the player's health stops dropping at `10` hearts, on **Normal**, it stops at `1` heart, and on **Hard**, it keeps draining until either the player eats something or starves to death. Resistance and armour do not reduce starvation damage

Switching to Peaceful difficulty eliminates all penalties above, and rapidly restores the player's hunger bar and health
.

👨‍🌾 Villagers 👨‍🌾

Author: iDexy and Zivkovic
Translator: Zivkovic
Writer: iDexy

In this channel we will talk about villagers and how you can use there trades to your advantage in PvP

Category 1: 📖 Basic Things 📖

- Villagers are passive mobs that inhabit villages, work at their professions, breed, and interact

- Their outfit varies according to their occupation and biome

- A player can trade with villagers using emeralds as currency

- Villagers can be found in villages, which spawn in several biomes such as plains, snowy tundras, savannas, deserts, taigas, and snowy taigas

- A cleric villager and cleric zombie villager spawn locked up in the basements of igloos (if the basement generates) under the carpet of the floor

- When a zombie villager is cured, it transforms into a villager, displaying purple Nausea status effect particles for 10 seconds after being cured

- A villager, either adult or baby, does not ordinarily drop any items or experience when killed. However, when a player holds an emerald or other item a villager is willing to trade for, the item it offers in trade appears in its hands. Killing the villager at such a time has a chance to cause it to drop the item it was holding

Upon successful trading, a villager drops 3–6 xp

Upon successful trading, while willing to breed, 8–11 xp is dropped

- Villagers run inside at night or during rain, closing doors behind them. They attempt to sleep at night, but if they cannot claim a bed, they stay indoors until morning. In the morning, they head outside and resume normal behavior. However, some villagers stay outside later than others unless being chased by an illager or zombie

- Villagers do not run away from skeletons (and their variants), spiders, or cave spiders since these hostile mobs are passive towards villagers, although a skeleton arrow might hit a villager by accident
.

Category 2: 🧙‍♀️ Variants 🧟

There are 4 variants of normal villagers:

1. Zombie Villagers - When a zombie kills a villager, it can turn the villager into a zombie villager, depending on the difficulty: 0% chance on easy, 50% chance on normal and 100% chance on hard. Zombie villagers also spawn naturally in the Overworld in the same conditions as a normal zombie, although much less commonly, with a 5% chance. Zombie villagers also spawn in abandoned villages and igloos (#combat-science Category 8 to get more information about difficulty)

2. Illagers - Illagers are hostile villager-like mobs that spawn in woodland mansions as well as pillager outposts, illager patrols, or raids. The varieties of illagers are vindicators, evokers, pillagers, and illusioners (which can be summoned only by using commands), along with two associated mobs: vexes and ravagers

Illagers are considered to be outcasts from villages, meaning they were once villagers, but turned evil, so the villagers kicked them out forever, leaving them the hatred of villagers. In addition to attacking players, they also attack villagers, wandering traders, and iron golems. They do not go seeking for villagers, and never naturally come to villages, except during raids and patrols (raids are explained below in Category 5)
.

3. Witches - Witches are hostile villager-like mobs that spawn anywhere in the Overworld in light levels of 7 or less, in swamp huts, as part of raids, or when a villager gets struck by lightning. Once a villager becomes a witch it cannot be turned back to a villager. Witches attack by throwing splash potions of harming, slowness, weakness and poison. They also use beneficial potions on themselves, especially healing potions when damaged, fire resistance potions if on fire, and water breathing potions if submerged in water. Witches in raids heal and buff illagers and other raider mobs by throwing beneficial potions and healing potions on them

Despite being allies with and looking similar in appearance to illagers, witches themselves are not considered illagers, are passive toward villagers and wandering traders, and are neutral toward iron golems. If a witch's negative splash potion hits a illager, the illager retaliates, leading to a fight

4. Wandering Traders - Wandering traders are a type of villager that spawn randomly close to the player. Two trader llamas spawn leashed to the wandering trader. Players may use emeralds to buy items from wandering traders, but cannot trade items for emeralds. They also lock trades like villagers, but never unlock the trade. Like villagers, wandering traders are attacked by most zombie variants (though they do not have a zombified form, they die if a zombie kills it), illagers, ravagers and vexes. Wandering traders also drink a Potion of Invisibility at night (or when they see a hostile mob such as an illager or zombie). They drink a milk bucket in the morning to remove the Invisibility. They despawn after 40-60 minutes (even with a name tag or in a minecart or boat). Wandering traders also spawn near bells
.

Category 3: 👨‍🌾 Professions 🧑‍🏭

Each villager can have a profession, indicated by their clothing as well as by the title at the top of the trading interface. A villager can choose their profession by claiming a job site block

What is a job site block and how it works?

Well, a job site block is a special block that allows the villager to get a job and restock his trades

An unemployed villager acquires a profession and a job by claiming the first unclaimed job site block it can detect in that area. A job site block can be detected as long as it is in range, not already claimed, and the villager can pathfind to the block to claim it. This means if they cannot see or get to the block, they cannot claim it

Employed villagers spend most of their day standing next to their job site blocks

There are 13 job site blocks corresponding with the villager professions:

(Crossed swords symbol ⚔️ means that the profession is important for pvp)
.

1. Blast Furnace (Armourer profession) ⚔️

2. Smoker (Butcher profession)

3. Cartography Table (Cartographer profession)

4. Brewing Stand (Cleric profession) ⚔️

5. Composter (Farmer profession) ⚔️

6. Barrel (Fisherman profession)

7. Fletching Table (Fletcher profession) ⚔️

8. Cauldron (Leatherworker profession)

9. Lectern (Librarian profession) ⚔️

10. Stoncecutter (Mason profession)

11. Loom (Shepherd profession)

12. Smithing Table (Toolsmith profession)

13. Grindstone (Weaponsmith profession)
.

So basically each villager can have a profession, indicated by their clothing as well as by the title at the top of the trading interface. A villager can choose their profession by claiming a job site block. When they go to work, they use their daily schedule to get to their claimed job site block. Some professions, like farmers and librarians, do other things. Farmers plant crops, and librarians can inspect bookshelves

Keep in mind that removal of a claimed job site block causes the owner to switch to another profession or become unemployed, provided that the villager has no prior trades with the player. If the villager has prior trades, it keeps its profession and claims a new job site block that matches its profession if one is available. So, once a player trades with a villager, the villager keeps its profession forever

There are other 2 professions that doesnt have a job site block:

1. Unemployed

2. Nitwit (Wear robes that are green on top. They cannot acquire a profession, trade, or gather around bells, but are still able to breed. They are not equipped with a level stone since they cannot trade)

Villagers have different outfits depending on their profession and the biome that they spawned in, you can take a look at them in the Minecraft Wiki (#references)
.

Category 4: 💰 Trading 💰

Basic Things:

- Each profession gives different types of items. As you trade with the villager it will level up and offer you better items but with a higher cost:

- Trading also gives exp points. If you trade a lot, it adds up and you get a ton of xp alongside the goods that you recieve from the villagers

- Xp is very important for combat as it allows you to enchant your armour and weapons. If you trade a lot, you can use the xp you got to combine the books you traded for with your armour

- Exp from trading is also a great way to take advantage of mending on your tools and armour, since it will get repaired as you trade

Farmer - Trades crops and natural foods

Fisherman - Trades campfires and fishing items

Shepherd - Trades shears, wool, dyes, paintings and beds

Fletcher - Trades bows, crossbows, all types of arrows (except luck) and archery ingredients

Cleric - Trades magic items like ender pearls, redstone dust, and enchanting or potion ingredients

Weaponsmith - Trades minerals, bells and enchanted melee weapons. The axe enchantments are weapon related

Armourer - Trades foundry items and sells chain, iron and enchanted diamond armor tiers

Toolsmith - Trades minerals, bells and harvest tools. The axe enchantments are tool related

Librarian - Trades enchanted books, clocks, compasses, name tags, glass, ink sacs, lanterns, and book and quills

Cartographer - Trades banners, compasses, banner patterns, papers and various maps, including explorer maps

Leatherworker - Trades scutes, rabbit hide, and leather-related items

Butcher - Trades meats, sweet berries, rabbit stew, and dried kelp blocks

Mason - Trades polished stones, terracotta, clay, glazed terracotta and quartz

Nitwit - No trades

Unemployed - No trades until employed. No badge until employed
.

- Their trades can be valuable or somewhat meaningless, depending on the cost, the items the player might get, and how the player treats the villagers. Only adult villagers with professions can trade; the player cannot trade with nitwits, unemployed villagers, or baby villagers

- Using an employed villager allows a player to trade, making offers based on the villager's profession and profession level

- All offers involve emeralds as a currency, and items related to the villager's profession. Trading can allow the acquisition of items that would otherwise be difficult or impossible to obtain, such as enchanted books with "treasure" enchantments (e.g. Mending), bottles o' enchanting, or chainmail armour etc

- Completing a trade with a villager increases its professional-level slightly. Some trades grant higher levels to the villager, while others do not. As it advances through its profession, the villager offers additional trades and when a villager unlocks a new trade at a higher level, it almost always grants more experience than every lower-level trade

- Villagers have a maximum supply of items and after the player has traded for an item that many times, the villager's supply of the item is exhausted. This results in the trade being temporarily locked. A player can continue to trade for the villager's other available items if any and exhausted items are restocked when the villager works at a job site, up to twice per day
.

Supply and Demand:

The price of an item can rise and fall with changes in demand. The price of a traded item can rise when next resupplied, or fall from a risen price if not traded. Demand is stored per item, not per villager

Economic Trade:

Villagers have levels and require experience to unlock the next tiers of trade; level 1 is a novice, level 2 is apprentice, level 3 is journeyman, level 4 is expert, and level 5 is master. Villagers can resupply trades by themselves by working more at their job site block
.

PvP Trades:

1. Librarian - They can give you enchanted books for everything besides soul speed, including protection 4, sharpness 5, power 5, mending, infinity, fire aspect 2, looting 3, feather falling 4, knockback 2, Depth strider 3, punch 2, flame and unbreaking 3

Great thing about librarians is that you don't need to level them up to get amazing books, their first trade could be, for example, a protection 4 or mending book

2. Armourer - At level 3, they can sell you shields. When at level 4, they give you diamond leggings and boots, and the chestplate and helmet at level 5. All the diamond gear will be randomly enchanted. At lower levels they sell iron and chain armour, so you can use them for that as well if you really cant find any iron

3. Farmer - At level 4, you can get a random suspicious stew from them which might
have a positive effect, and at level 5, they sell golden carrots, which are great for combat because of their high saturation (for regen) while also restoring a good amount of hunger points. At lvl 5 they also sell glistering melons(used to make health potions)

4. Cleric - At level 2, they sell lapis lazuli (used at enchant tables). At level 3, they sell glowstone(to power respawn anchors). At level 4, they might sell you ender pearls, and at 5 they might sell exp bottles (for repairing mending armour)

5. Fletcher - At level 1, they might sell you arrows. At level 2 they sell bows(enchanted ones at level 4), at level 3 crossbows(enchanted ones at level 5). At level 5, they will sell you a random tipped arrow

❗ IMPORTANT ❗

- Weaponwmiths can sell enchanted dia swords and axes, but imo its not worth the time it takes to level them up, better to just mine for your weapons)
.

Hero of the Village (Discounts and Gifts):

Players receive gifts‌ and discounts from villager trades while under the effect (#effects Category 4 if you wanna know more things about this effect)

When you have hero of the village, villagers will throw random gifts at you, some of which may help you in combat, such as chain armour, food, tipped arrows, and axes. Also players receive discounted prices on all the items traded by villagers

Curing a villager from being zombified gives significant permanent discounts, and can be done up to 5 times to maximize it
.

Category 5: ⚔️ Raids ⚔️

(#effects Category 4 if you wanna know about omen effect)

During a raid, villagers flee from illagers and run to the nearest house, similar to a zombie siege. For a villager to hide, the house must have a door and at least one bed

Before the first raid wave , at least one villager rushes to ring the bell in the center of the village (if they are close enough) to warn the other villagers of an incoming raid before going into their house

A villager often stays in the house it first entered, but may exit the house occasionally. The player can still trade with villagers during a raid

Once the player gains the Hero of the Village status after defeating a raid, villagers give them a discount for their trades and throw them gifts related to their profession

Fighting raids is beneficial since you can farm totems with them, and also get discounts and gifts from the villagers!

Totems are dropped by evokers:

.
In wave 5 only 1 shows up, if u wanna get more totems u have to do more waves
.

Category 6: 💡 Villagers Tips 💡

Here you can see some tips about villagers that can help you in some decisions and games:

- Use hard difficulty when zombifying and curing villagers, on other difficulties they may just die instead of becoming a zombie

- Cure each villager twice, it lowers most prices down to 1 and doesn't cost too much gold

- If you have a tool with mending that needs to be repaired, hold it while trading, so the xp you get will repair it

- If you have cartographers that have been cured twice, at lvl 2 you get a trade of 1 glass pane for 1 emerald

Trade with a librarian 3 times for 4 glass, each trade is 1 emerald. so you spend 3 emeralds and get 12 glass. Then turn that glass to 32 panes, and you can trade it to the cartographers and just like that you spend 3 emeralds but gain 32. You can repeat this trick infinitely to gain a lot of emeralds quickly

- When mining take as much coal and iron as you can, these can be used to trade with and level up the blacksmith type villagers. This is especially useful if they are not cured.
.

- If you break a workstation, if you haven't traded with the villager yet it will lose its job. Then you can replace it and the villager will reclaim it and get another set of trades so you can keep rerolling until you get what you want. This is especially useful with librarians when you're trying to get a specific enchantment

- Fletcher villagers buy sticks which can be obtained easily and sold for emeralds

**Author:** `iDexy and Zivkovic`
**Translator:** `Zivkovic`
**Writer:** `iDexy`

In this channel we will talk about villagers and how you can use there trades to your advantage in PvP

***Category 1:*** 📖 `Basic Things` 📖 

`-` Villagers are passive mobs that inhabit villages, work at their professions, breed, and interact

`-` Their outfit varies according to their occupation and biome

`-` A player can trade with villagers using emeralds as currency

`-` Villagers can be found in villages, which spawn in several biomes such as plains, snowy tundras, savannas, deserts, taigas, and snowy taigas

`-` A cleric villager and cleric zombie villager spawn locked up in the basements of igloos (if the basement generates) under the carpet of the floor

`-` When a zombie villager is cured, it transforms into a villager, displaying purple Nausea status effect particles for `10 seconds` after being cured

`-` A villager, either adult or baby, does not ordinarily drop any items or experience when killed. However, when a player holds an emerald or other item a villager is willing to trade for, the item it offers in trade appears in its hands. Killing the villager at such a time has a chance to cause it to drop the item it was holding

> Upon successful trading, a villager drops 3–6 xp
> 
> Upon successful trading, while willing to breed, 8–11 xp is dropped

`-` Villagers run inside at night or during rain, closing doors behind them. They attempt to sleep at night, but if they cannot claim a bed, they stay indoors until morning. In the morning, they head outside and resume normal behavior. However, some villagers stay outside later than others unless being chased by an illager or zombie

`-` Villagers do not run away from skeletons (and their variants), spiders, or cave spiders since these hostile mobs are passive towards villagers, although a skeleton arrow might hit a villager by accident
.

***Category 2:***  🧙‍♀️ `Variants` 🧟

There are `4` variants of normal villagers:

`1.` **Zombie Villagers** - When a zombie kills a villager, it can turn the villager into a zombie villager, depending on the difficulty: `0%` chance on easy, `50%` chance on normal and `100%` chance on hard. Zombie villagers also spawn naturally in the Overworld in the same conditions as a normal zombie, although much less commonly, with a 5% chance. Zombie villagers also spawn in abandoned villages and igloos (**<#842456718452719676> Category 8** to get more information about difficulty)

`2.` **Illagers** -  Illagers are hostile villager-like mobs that spawn in woodland mansions as well as pillager outposts, illager patrols, or raids. The varieties of illagers are vindicators, evokers, pillagers, and illusioners (which can be summoned only by using commands), along with two associated mobs: vexes and ravagers

Illagers are considered to be outcasts from villages, meaning they were once villagers, but turned evil, so the villagers kicked them out forever, leaving them the hatred of villagers. In addition to attacking players, they also attack villagers, wandering traders, and iron golems. They do not go seeking for villagers, and never naturally come to villages, except during raids and patrols (raids are explained below in **Category 5**)
.

`3.` **Witches** - Witches are hostile villager-like mobs that spawn anywhere in the Overworld in light levels of `7` or less, in swamp huts, as part of raids, or when a villager gets struck by lightning. Once a villager becomes a witch it cannot be turned back to a villager. Witches attack by throwing splash potions of harming, slowness, weakness and poison. They also use beneficial potions on themselves, especially healing potions when damaged, fire resistance potions if on fire, and water breathing potions if submerged in water. Witches in raids heal and buff illagers and other raider mobs by throwing beneficial potions and healing potions on them

Despite being allies with and looking similar in appearance to illagers, witches themselves are not considered illagers, are passive toward villagers and wandering traders, and are neutral toward iron golems. If a witch's negative splash potion hits a illager, the illager retaliates, leading to a fight

`4.` **Wandering Traders** - Wandering traders are a type of villager that spawn randomly close to the player. Two trader llamas spawn leashed to the wandering trader. Players may use emeralds to buy items from wandering traders, but cannot trade items for emeralds. They also lock trades like villagers, but never unlock the trade. Like villagers, wandering traders are attacked by most zombie variants (though they do not have a zombified form, they die if a zombie kills it), illagers, ravagers and vexes. Wandering traders also drink a Potion of Invisibility at night (or when they see a hostile mob such as an illager or zombie). They drink a milk bucket in the morning to remove the Invisibility. They despawn after `40-60 minutes` (even with a name tag or in a minecart or boat). Wandering traders also spawn near bells
.

***Category 3:*** 👨‍🌾 `Professions` 🧑‍🏭 

Each villager can have a profession, indicated by their clothing as well as by the title at the top of the trading interface. A villager can choose their profession by claiming a job site block

**What is a job site block and how it works?**

Well, a job site block is a special block that allows the villager to get a job and restock his trades

An unemployed villager acquires a profession and a job by claiming the first unclaimed job site block it can detect in that area. A job site block can be detected as long as it is in range, not already claimed, and the villager can pathfind to the block to claim it. This means if they cannot see or get to the block, they cannot claim it

Employed villagers spend most of their day standing next to their job site blocks

There are `13` job site blocks corresponding with the villager professions:

(Crossed swords symbol ⚔️  means that the profession is important for pvp)
.

`1.` **Blast Furnace** (Armourer profession) ⚔️ 

`2.` **Smoker** (Butcher profession)

`3.` **Cartography Table** (Cartographer profession)

`4.` **Brewing Stand** (Cleric profession) ⚔️ 

`5.` **Composter** (Farmer profession) ⚔️ 

`6.` **Barrel** (Fisherman profession)

`7.` **Fletching Table** (Fletcher profession) ⚔️ 

`8.` **Cauldron** (Leatherworker profession)

`9.` **Lectern** (Librarian profession) ⚔️ 

`10.` **Stoncecutter** (Mason profession)

`11.` **Loom** (Shepherd profession)

`12.` **Smithing Table** (Toolsmith profession)

`13.` **Grindstone** (Weaponsmith profession)
.

A villager can choose their profession by claiming a job site block. When they go to work, they use their daily schedule to get to their claimed job site block. Some professions, like farmers and librarians, do other things. Farmers plant crops, and librarians can inspect bookshelves

If the villager has prior trades, it keeps its profession and claims a new job site block that matches its profession if one is available. So, once a player trades with a villager, the villager keeps its profession forever

`1.` **Unemployed**

`2.` **Nitwit** (Wear robes that are green on top. They cannot acquire a profession, trade, or gather around bells, but are still able to breed. They are not equipped with a level stone since they cannot trade)

.

`Toolsmith` - Trades minerals, bells and harvest tools. The axe enchantments are tool related

`Librarian` - Trades enchanted books, clocks, compasses, name tags, glass, ink sacs, lanterns, and book and quills

`Cartographer` - Trades banners, compasses, banner patterns, papers and various maps, including explorer maps

`Leatherworker` - Trades scutes, rabbit hide, and leather-related items

`Butcher` - Trades meats, sweet berries, rabbit stew, and dried kelp blocks

`Mason` - Trades polished stones, terracotta, clay, glazed terracotta and quartz

As it advances through its profession, the villager offers additional trades and when a villager unlocks a new trade at a higher level, it almost always grants more experience than every lower-level trade

This results in the trade being temporarily locked. A player can continue to trade for the villager's other available items if any and exhausted items are restocked when the villager works at a job site, up to twice per day
.

The price of an item can rise and fall with changes in demand. The price of a traded item can rise when next resupplied, or fall from a risen price if not traded. Demand is stored per item, not per villager

Villagers have levels and require experience to unlock the next tiers of trade; level 1 is a novice, level 2 is apprentice, level 3 is journeyman, level 4 is expert, and level 5 is master. Villagers can resupply trades by themselves by working more at their job site block
.

**Great thing about librarians is that you don't need to level them up to get amazing books, their first trade could be, for example, a protection 4 or mending book**

`2.` **Armourer** - At level 3, they can sell you shields. When at level 4, they give you diamond leggings and boots, and the chestplate and helmet at level 5. All the diamond gear will be randomly enchanted. At lower levels they sell iron and chain armour, so you can use them for that as well if you really cant find any iron

`3.` **Farmer** - At level 4, you can get a random suspicious stew from them which might 
 have a positive effect, and at level 5, they sell golden carrots, which are great for combat because of their high saturation (for regen) while also restoring a good amount of hunger points. At lvl 5 they also sell glistering melons(used to make health potions)

`4.` **Cleric** - At level 2, they sell lapis lazuli (used at enchant tables). At level 3, they sell glowstone(to power respawn anchors). At level 4, they might sell you ender pearls, and at 5 they might sell exp bottles (for repairing mending armour)

`5.` **Fletcher** - At level 1, they might sell you arrows. At level 2 they sell bows(enchanted ones at level 4), at level 3 crossbows(enchanted ones at level 5). At level 5, they will sell you a random tipped arrow

❗ **__IMPORTANT__** ❗ 

`-` Weaponwmiths can sell enchanted dia swords and axes, but imo its not worth the time it takes to level them up, better to just mine for your weapons)
.

Players receive gifts‌ and discounts from villager trades while under the effect (**<#859903976422244392> Category 4** if you wanna know more things about this effect)

When you have hero of the village, villagers will throw random gifts at you, some of which may help you in combat, such as chain armour, food, tipped arrows, and axes. Also players receive discounted prices on all the items traded by villagers

Curing a villager from being zombified gives significant permanent discounts, and can be done up to 5 times to maximize it
.

(**<#859903976422244392> Category 4** if you wanna know about omen effect)

During a raid, villagers flee from illagers and run to the nearest house, similar to a zombie siege. For a villager to hide, the house must have a door and at least one bed

Before the first raid wave , at least one villager rushes to ring the bell in the center of the village (if they are close enough) to warn the other villagers of an incoming raid before going into their house

A villager often stays in the house it first entered, but may exit the house occasionally. The player can still trade with villagers during a raid

Once the player gains the Hero of the Village status after defeating a raid, villagers give them a discount for their trades and throw them gifts related to their profession

.
In wave 5 only 1 shows up, if u wanna get more totems u have to do more waves
.

Here you can see some tips about villagers that can help you in some decisions and games:

`-` Cure each villager twice, it lowers most prices down to 1 and doesn't cost too much gold

Then turn that glass to 32 panes, and you can trade it to the cartographers and just like that you spend 3 emeralds but gain 32. You can repeat this trick infinitely to gain a lot of emeralds quickly

.

Then you can replace it and the villager will reclaim it and get another set of trades so you can keep rerolling until you get what you want. messages.author: iDexy
messages.sourceText:
**Supply and Demand:**

The price of an item can rise and fall with changes in demand. The price of a traded item can rise when next resupplied, or fall from a risen price if not traded. Demand is stored per item, not per villager

**Economic Trade:**

Villagers have levels and require experience to unlock the next tiers of trade; level 1 is a novice, level 2 is apprentice, level 3 is journeyman, level 4 is expert, and level 5 is master. Villagers can resupply trades by themselves by working more at their job site block
.

messages.author: iDexy
messages.sourceText:
**PvP Trades:**

`1.` **Librarian** - They can give you enchanted books for everything besides soul speed, including protection 4, sharpness 5, power 5, mending, infinity, fire aspect 2, looting 3, feather falling 4, knockback 2, Depth strider 3, punch 2, flame and unbreaking 3

**Great thing about librarians is that you don't need to level them up to get amazing books, their first trade could be, for example, a protection 4 or mending book**

`2.` **Armourer** - At level 3, they can sell you shields. When at level 4, they give you diamond leggings and boots, and the chestplate and helmet at level 5. All the diamond gear will be randomly enchanted. At lower levels they sell iron and chain armour, so you can use them for that as well if you really cant find any iron

`3.` **Farmer** - At level 4, you can get a random suspicious stew from them which might 
 have a positive effect, and at level 5, they sell golden carrots, which are great for combat because of their high saturation (for regen) while also restoring a good amount of hunger points. At lvl 5 they also sell glistering melons(used to make health potions)

`4.` **Cleric** - At level 2, they sell lapis lazuli (used at enchant tables). At level 3, they sell glowstone(to power respawn anchors). At level 4, they might sell you ender pearls, and at 5 they might sell exp bottles (for repairing mending armour)

`5.` **Fletcher** - At level 1, they might sell you arrows. At level 2 they sell bows(enchanted ones at level 4), at level 3 crossbows(enchanted ones at level 5). At level 5, they will sell you a random tipped arrow

❗ **__IMPORTANT__** ❗ 

`-` Weaponwmiths can sell enchanted dia swords and axes, but imo its not worth the time it takes to level them up, better to just mine for your weapons)
.

messages.author: iDexy
messages.sourceText:
**Hero of the Village (Discounts and Gifts):**

Players receive gifts‌ and discounts from villager trades while under the effect (**<#859903976422244392> Category 4** if you wanna know more things about this effect)

When you have hero of the village, villagers will throw random gifts at you, some of which may help you in combat, such as chain armour, food, tipped arrows, and axes. Also players receive discounted prices on all the items traded by villagers

Curing a villager from being zombified gives significant permanent discounts, and can be done up to 5 times to maximize it
.

messages.author: iDexy
messages.sourceText:
***Category 5:*** ⚔️ `Raids` ⚔️ 

(**<#859903976422244392> Category 4** if you wanna know about omen effect)

During a raid, villagers flee from illagers and run to the nearest house, similar to a zombie siege. For a villager to hide, the house must have a door and at least one bed

Before the first raid wave , at least one villager rushes to ring the bell in the center of the village (if they are close enough) to warn the other villagers of an incoming raid before going into their house

A villager often stays in the house it first entered, but may exit the house occasionally. The player can still trade with villagers during a raid

Once the player gains the Hero of the Village status after defeating a raid, villagers give them a discount for their trades and throw them gifts related to their profession

**Fighting raids is beneficial since you can farm totems with them, and also get discounts and gifts from the villagers!**

Totems are dropped by evokers:

messages.author: iDexy
messages.sourceText:
.
In wave 5 only 1 shows up, if u wanna get more totems u have to do more waves
.

messages.author: iDexy
messages.sourceText:
***Category 6:*** 💡 `Villagers Tips` 💡 

Here you can see some tips about villagers that can help you in some decisions and games:

`-` Use hard difficulty when zombifying and curing villagers, on other difficulties they may just die instead of becoming a zombie

`-` Cure each villager twice, it lowers most prices down to 1 and doesn't cost too much gold

`-` If you have a tool with mending that needs to be repaired, hold it while trading, so the xp you get will repair it

`-` If you have cartographers that have been cured twice, at lvl 2 you get a trade of 1 glass pane for 1 emerald

Trade with a librarian 3 times for 4 glass, each trade is 1 emerald. so you spend 3 emeralds and get 12 glass. Then turn that glass to 32 panes, and you can trade it to the cartographers and just like that you spend 3 emeralds but gain 32. You can repeat this trick infinitely to gain a lot of emeralds quickly

`-` When mining take as much coal and iron as you can, these can be used to trade with and level up the blacksmith type villagers. This is especially useful if they are not cured.
.

messages.author: iDexy
messages.sourceText:
`-` If you break a workstation, if you haven't traded with the villager yet it will lose its job.  Then you can replace it and the villager will reclaim it and get another set of trades so you can keep rerolling until you get what you want. This is especially useful with librarians when you're trying to get a specific enchantment

`-` Fletcher villagers buy sticks which can be obtained easily and sold for emeralds
